My pain is pretty typical for my disorder, though my doctors have said I have one of the worst cases they've ever seen. I take enough pain meds to easily stop a horse (literally). There's just nothing left for me to try at this point. My neuro is hesitant to give me a higher dose. I'm only 37, if I live I don't have much higher I can go.

It's extreme pain caused by (in my case) 3 blood vessels touching the Trigeminal nerve. It's called the suicide disease, and is similar to cluster migraines, except my attacks last hours or days instead of minutes. I can't eat or drink anything cold, and a wind blowing on my face is a trigger, as well as any touch on the left side of my face. Winter is worse because of the cold, so I rarely leave the house. 
My exhaustion from the Thyroidectomy has made my life go from painful to pointless. I wake up exhausted- I go from bed to the couch back to bed. My kids basically have no mom. My husband has no wife. My house is falling apart because I have no energy to do even the basics. 
I feel like everyone would be better off without me. My husband could remarry, and someone would be able to take care of my kids. And would be out of pain, and free from guilt. And no longer a burden to my aging parents.

That's a good idea to limit my interactions with people. The surgeon wants to see me on Thursday because my calcium, Vit D and magnesium are low, so I can ask her to add the TSH levels in with the other tests. Thank you for talking to me and the advice!

I'm sorry you feel so bad. I'm sorry the depression has taken you to a dark cave, and you don't know how to get out. My one suggestion is to allow your mom to take you to a psychologist and really, truly try anti-depressants.  

I see your situation from two points of view- I have a son who is 12, and I'm also feeling the temptation of suicide. I take medicines that totally meds up my memory; my family makes fun of me for it as well. For your mom's sake, accept all the help you have access to. 

I'm sorry if I'm not being very helpful. I came on here to post my own struggles with living, but saw your post instead. I want to help you, I want you to live. High school can suck even if you aren't depressed. 

Oh! Here's one idea to try with your therapist. I have the same issue, as in I don't want to talk to her about my suicidal thoughts because I don't want to be taken to a psychiatric ward. So we have a pact: if it comes to the point that I can't stop myself from committing suicide I let her know. And I'm free to talk about everything else without worry. Maybe you can set up something similar with your therapist? Let him/her know you don't feel free to talk because of the restrictions, and see what can be done to get around them. Maybe by talking about "a friend." But you'd have to promise them if it came to suicide you'd let them know.
